correctness.rationale: Each rim component of length ℓ<n containing a root vertex has probability ℓ(a/n)^2(1-a/n)^(ℓ-1); the whole rim is one component precisely with 0 or 1 failed rim edges, probability (1-a/n)^n+n(a/n)(1-a/n)^(n-1). Missing all ℓ spokes has probability (1-b/n)^ℓ, giving finite mean; zero hub fraction iff no spokes. Independent Bernoulli lattice cut and spoke processes converge jointly to independent Poisson circle processes, and the marked arc-mass functional is a.s. continuous away from collisions. For full mass, cyclic merged label words have no adjacent cut labels and at least one spoke, with transfer M=[[b,a],[b,0]] and exponential trace sum for m>=1 giving the stated two eigenvalue formula. A uniformly chosen point lies in a unit arc with probability (1+a)e^-a, otherwise size-biased arc length density a² ℓ e^-aℓ on (0,1), giving E H=1-(1+a)e^-(a+b)-a²/(a+b)²[1-(1+a+b)e^-(a+b)]. Exactly two cuts and marks on just one arc yield positive interior mass. Independent full 2n-edge enumeration n=3..6 at two rational rate pairs verifies finite mean and zero mass.

Qualified PASS for an explicit two-rate, root-specific, growing-wheel critical window with Poisson arc-mark distribution, both boundary atoms and exact means. Existing Mann et al work analyzes percolation giant components of random ensembles containing homogeneous cycle/clique motifs and uses common edge occupation, not the same root-specific opposite critical rim/spoke scaling. Allard et al broadly handle finite arbitrary graphs and thus can calculate each fixed wheel, but a general finite recursion does not directly present the Poisson scaling limit and transfer-matrix boundary masses. Classical circle-covering theory may contain equivalent marked-spacing probabilities.
